clue.text: What one tells travel, ling builder to be prepared for army discipline

definitions.text: What one tells travel, ling builder to be prepared
definitions.meaning: a travelling builder getting ready would be told to put his drill in his bag
a punishment of marching up and down in full kit

explanation.surface: Instructions for a builder on the move, set beside the rigours of military punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text splits 'travelling' with a stray comma. The first reading is an order to a tradesman: get your tool packed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the military punishment of drilling in full marching kit, a classic form of army discipline.

clue.text: Improved after being reprimanded

definitions.meaning: trade or health that has got better has recovered or risen
to be pulled up or corrected for a fault

explanation.surface: Someone whose performance got better once they had been told off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both recovered or rallied and, of a person, corrected or rebuked for an error.

clue.text: Cleaner has children with irresistible appeal

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning lady, short for charwoman
someone with children is a ma, a mother, read as 'is ma'

explanation.surface: A domestic cleaner with a family is found to be utterly charming.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR is an everyday British word for a cleaning woman. 'Has children' is read whimsically as IS MA, that is, is a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal magnetism or compelling attractiveness that draws others to someone.

clue.text: Lawyer admits damage by Indian custom

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the lawyer's letters take in the damage

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
harm means damage or injury

explanation.surface: A lawyer concedes that harm was done by a custom in India.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist thought this is the moral law and right conduct that governs life, a customary duty.

clue.text: Eventually played at the correct tempo

definitions.meaning: sooner or later, given enough time
musicians keeping to the beat are said to be playing to the rhythm

explanation.surface: Music that was finally performed at the right speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'after a while, ultimately' and also 'keeping to the beat' in music.

clue.text: Ally is to be used in the sovereign's service

indicators.note: the letters are to be put to use in a fresh order, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A friend who is employed on behalf of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be used' tells you to rearrange ALLY IS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the Crown, faithful to the monarch, especially in time of rebellion.

clue.text: Exemplary healer induced to return

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a military doctor

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for induced reads backwards

parts.note: led means persuaded or induced

explanation.surface: A doctor is persuaded to come back to work.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means ideal or perfect, worthy of being copied.

clue.text: Contemplate having friend around to make corrections

indicators.note: the word for a friend goes round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: mate is British slang for a friend
edit means to correct a text

explanation.surface: Pondering whether to have a pal help with proofreading.
explanation.definitionFit: To think deeply or reflect quietly on something.

clue.text: Socialite scoffed in discussion

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young society woman
to scoff is British slang for eating greedily

explanation.surface: A society girl gobbled her food during an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' here is British slang for ate greedily, not mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument or exchange of opposing views.

clue.text: Probably 51,000 needed by English cathedral

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals and K stands for a thousand
Ely is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Roughly fifty-one thousand pounds required by an English cathedral, at a guess.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a small city in Cambridgeshire famous for its cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means in all probability, very possibly.

clue.text: About to thrash worker for calling aloud

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
lam means to beat or thrash
an ant is the classic crossword worker insect

explanation.surface: Someone about to beat an employee for shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means noisy or insistently demanding, clamouring for attention.

clue.text: Foolishly maintain oriental 19 without vitality

indicators.note: done foolishly, the letters are shuffled into a silly order

parts.note: E for east, the oriental direction

explanation.surface: Stupidly keeping an Eastern object that has no life in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan's '19' is a misread of 'is', a link word. 'Foolishly' rearranges MAINTAIN to INANIMAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless, lacking spirit or animation, like an object rather than a living being.

clue.text: Daughter is to relax following illness

parts.note: ease means to relax or loosen

explanation.surface: A daughter is to take it easy after being ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickness or disorder of body or mind.

clue.text: I have permission to include German symbolism

indicators.note: including something means holding it within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: may expresses being allowed to

explanation.surface: Someone allowed to take in a German speaks of their symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative language or visual symbols used in art or writing.

clue.text: CID officer is no dandy

definitions.meaning: a detective of the Criminal Investigation Department, who works out of uniform
someone who dresses simply rather than showily

explanation.surface: A detective is far from a fashionable dresser.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: A police detective who wears ordinary dress instead of uniform, and literally a fellow in unremarkable garments.

clue.text: No male interrupts mass meeting as a rule

indicators.note: breaking into the middle of something, so one letter cuts the meeting word open

parts.note: a rally is a large public gathering

explanation.surface: No man breaks up a big demonstration, as is usually the case.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually, under ordinary circumstances.

clue.text: Linguist demands "Can I come in at the end?"

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so these letters go inside the word for the end

parts.note: last means final, the end
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A language expert asks whether they may come in at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of the language of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Principal occupation for the railway company?

parts.note: main means chief or principal
one's line is one's line of work, an occupation

explanation.surface: Working for a railway as one's chief job.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal trunk route of a railway network, the core of the company's service.

clue.text: Uncalled-for advice to the overindulgent

definitions.meaning: telling a glutton to require a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Unwanted counsel offered to people who eat too much.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means unnecessary, and split in two it tells a glutton to cut back.

clue.text: French philosopher died in torment? Rubbish!

indicators.note: letters in torment are twisted out of shape, signalling an anagram

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a French thinker died in agony is dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot was the eighteenth-century French thinker who edited the Encyclopédie.

clue.text: Edward returned pipe to get discount

indicators.note: sent back, so the short name reads in the opposite direction

parts.note: Ed is a short form of Edward
a duct is a pipe or channel

explanation.surface: Edward sent a pipe back to obtain a reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: To take away an amount from a total, as when giving a reduction.

clue.text: Frustrated by seeing woman in pa's embrace

indicators.note: the woman sits inside the father word
an embrace encloses, so the father's word wraps round the woman

parts.note: pa is another word for dad
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone thwarted at the sight of a woman in her father's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes that are dashed are thwarted or crushed.

clue.text: Young lady, I have to prepare a letter

parts.note: miss is a title for a young unmarried woman
I've contracts I have

explanation.surface: A girl says she must draft some correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal or lengthy written message.

clue.text: Frenchwoman forced to take in a Frenchman

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the word for forced encloses the rest

parts.note: made means compelled or forced
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman compelled to give shelter to a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title for a married woman, hence a Frenchwoman.

clue.text: A scene set by Roman dramatist

indicators.note: letters that are set are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A stage scene arranged by a classical playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger wrote tragedies in first-century Rome.

clue.text: Sid, Ed and I went mad when treated scornfully

indicators.note: going mad means losing order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Three friends lost their heads when they were looked down on.
explanation.definitionFit: Regarded with contempt, looked down upon.

clue.text: Fish for the landlord's lady?

definitions.meaning: a pub landlord's partner, a woman who keeps an alehouse

explanation.surface: A fish served up for the publican's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: A British landlord here is the keeper of a pub, so his lady is his wife at the alehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a kind of herring and, historically, a woman who ran a tavern.

clue.text: Sweetened alcohol is divine in trifle

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, something of little value
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a clergyman or divine

explanation.surface: A sweet drink turns out to be heavenly in a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' suggests the British layered dessert but means a plaything; 'divine' is a clergyman, DD.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot drink of spirits mixed with water, sugar and spices.

clue.text: Youth generates disruption

indicators.note: disruption throws the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Young people cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectively, young people in their adolescent years.
